title: POC hosting decision criteria & workloads — Orchid Systems kickoff
topics: Deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to validate hosting mode for Orchid Systems' conversational summarization product. Agreement to run throughput + latency benchmarks on representative traffic and a privacy/regulatory checklist. Main decision hinges on predictable tail latency vs data residency and key management needs. Redwood to provide benchmark plan and security docs; customer to supply traffic traces and success metrics.
action_items: Tom Gallagher | Provide representative production traffic profile (2 weeks) + sample request/response traces | 2027-01-04
Mateo Ruiz | Share benchmark harness and initial benchmark script (throughput/99th/median) and instructions | 2026-12-23
Alicia Park | Send Redwood POC SOW template, rough pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated | 2026-12-22
Sara Kim | Compile a list of required compliance controls (data residency, KMS, SOC2 evidence) and stakeholder contacts | 2027-01-06
next_steps: Redwood to run a baseline hosted benchmark against a small sample trace and share results

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 15:30 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Orchid), Tom Gallagher (Head of ML), Sara Kim (Infra), Ethan Lowe (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Redwood and Orchid aligned on running a 4-6 week POC, focus on throughput/latency and security. Workload sizing is around 150 QPS peak with spiky tails; Orchid has strict data residency needs for EU customers. Decision factors: latency SLOs, cost per token, dedicated pools for predictable tail latency, and private deployment for air-gapped use cases. Action items assigned.

Topics: Success criteria; Workload sizing; Benchmarks (99th/median throughput); Hosting tradeoffs; Security (K M S, SOC 2); Timeline and gating.

[00:00] Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alicia from Redwood, I lead the AE team. We also have Mateo who is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Doing well, thanks. Busy end of quarter but happy to be here.
[00:12] Tom Gallagher: Hey, morning for us. Tom here. We want to focus on the hosting tradeoffs — whether we can go hosted for speed or need dedicated or private.
[00:20] Alicia Park: Totally, that is the goal. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, understand traffic and sizing, pick benchmark metrics, and agree a timeline. Mateo will cover the benchmark harness and what we need to run.
[00:31] Mateo Ruiz: Hi all. Quick note, I'll be fairly technical — I'll ask about sequence lengths, KV cache behavior, and tail latency requirements. Also we'll propose a small harness that measures median, p95 and p99, and a cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[00:45] Ethan Lowe: For product context: our summarization API averages 220 tokens output, 600 tokens input. We have a bursty user base — weekends spike and end-of-day spikes. Peak short-term QPS we've seen is about 150 QPS, sustained about 20 QPS.
[01:02] Sara Kim: And infra-wise we need EU data residency and K M S for key management. We can't ship raw logs out of our VPC without masking.
[01:12] Alicia Park: Good, that's a clear constraint. Is SOC 2 or any specific certs required?
[01:16] Priya Nair: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 would be the nice-to-haves, but SOC 2 is required for contracts with our enterprise partners. Also SSO via SAML — single sign-on for the console is a must.
[01:29] Mateo Ruiz: Redwood supports SAML SSO and we can integrate with your existing IdP. On the hosting side, let me outline tradeoffs quickly: Hosted = fastest onboarding, lower ops for you, but multi-tenant so limited control over underlying infra. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, more predictable p99 latency and isolation. Private = full control, VPC or on-prem install for air-gapped compliance but longer setup and ops.
[01:55] Tom Gallagher: Can we quantify what "predictable p99" looks like on Dedicated vs Hosted? Like, what's the difference in ms?
[02:02] Mateo Ruiz: Ballpark: for our curated smaller models, hosted p99 might be in the 350–700ms range depending on sequence length and load; dedicated pools tuned for your workload can bring p99 down to 120–250ms because we can allocate fewer co-tenants and tune kernels/quantization. Those numbers are noisy — benchmark will give better numbers.
[02:25] Priya Nair: Cost-wise, how do we think about per-request cost vs committed seats? Our CFO will want to model committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go.
[02:33] Alicia Park: We generally provide both options. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commitment. We can run a cost-sensitivity analysis after we get baseline throughput and token counts. We'll send a sample pricing sheet after the call.
[02:48] Ethan Lowe: For the POC, our success criteria would be: 1) latency below 300ms p95 for EU users, 2) <1% error rate, 3) end-to-end availability 99.5% during the pilot, and 4) data residency and encryption compliance checks — would that be reasonable?
[03:07] Mateo Ruiz: That seems reasonable. We generally recommend including p99 as well for tail behavior since conversational workloads are sensitive to spikes. Maybe: p95 <300ms and p99 <500ms as a POC target for Hosted; if we can't meet that we test Dedicated variant.
[03:23] Tom Gallagher: How invasive is the benchmark? Do you need full production traffic or sampled traces?
[03:28] Mateo Ruiz: Ideally we'd take two weeks of request traces and replay them through our harness. If that's not possible, a representative sample with realistic token distributions and burst patterns works. We'll need per-request token counts, latency tolerances, and any special operations like function calling.
[03:45] Sara Kim: We'll need to scrub PII before sharing traces — is there a recommended process?
[03:49] Mateo Ruiz: Yes — strip or hash user IDs, mask sensitive fields. We can provide a small script to anonymize logs.
[03:58] Alicia Park: I'll attach the anonymizer script with the benchmark harness and instructions.
[04:02] Priya Nair: On the Private option, can Redwood support an on-prem deployment or is it only VPC-hosted?
[04:08] Mateo Ruiz: We support both Private VPC deployments and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. On-prem requires deeper engagements — installation, HW procurement, and typically a 4–8 week setup.
[04:22] Tom Gallagher: That setup time is a bit long for our pilot. We might only include Private if a partner contract requires it. For the POC, we prefer Hosted first, then test Dedicated if we hit tail latency issues.
[04:36] Alicia Park: Makes sense. For the benchmark plan, we propose three phases: 1) baseline hosted run against a 1-day sample (sanitized) within 48–72 hours; 2) 2-week replay to capture burst patterns; 3) optional dedicated pool run comparing p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates.
[05:00] Ethan Lowe: That timeline seems fine. Who owns phase 1 data prep?
[05:03] Tom Gallagher: I'll own the trace extraction and scrub with Sara's help.
[05:07] Sara Kim: Yup. We'll deliver an anonymized trace and a short doc describing traffic patterns.
[05:11] Mateo Ruiz: For the harness we'll need: average and max sequence lengths, tokenizer details (we saw 600 tokens avg input), any custom tokens, and concurrency distribution.
[05:20] Tom Gallagher: We'll include that. One question: do you support automatic KV cache reuse for conversational flows? We have long contexts for multi-turns.
[05:27] Mateo Ruiz: Yes we support KV cache handling and prefix caching strategies — though the benchmark needs to simulate the actual cache hit rates. If your app uses persistent per-user caches, let us know typical hit rates.
[05:35] Priya Nair: Security checklist — we need to validate K M S integration and that we can bring our own keys. Also audit logs with at least 90-day retention, and RBAC integrated with our IdP.
[05:47] Alicia Park: Redwood supports BYOK via common KMS providers and can ship audit logs to your SIEM. We'll include a security doc and evidence pack.
[05:54] Ethan Lowe: Another commercial question: if we do Dedicated, can we burst to hosted for spikes?
[06:00] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we offer burst policies so Dedicated customers can configure a fallback to hosted or a different capacity tier for spikes. There are tradeoffs on data plane routing and residency when bursting across regions — we'll document those.
[06:13] Tom Gallagher: Important: EU-only traffic must remain in EU. Bursting to hosted US infra is not acceptable for those requests.
[06:20] Mateo Ruiz: Understood; we can set region-bound routing policies and fallbacks that only use EU capacity.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Can Redwood provide a simple pass/fail for regulatory gating? Something like a short checklist for us to sign off?
[06:34] Alicia Park: Yes, we'll include a compliance checklist which your legal/security teams can sign off on. It will include K M S, SOC 2 artifacts, data residency, logging, and SSO/RBAC.
[06:46] Ethan Lowe: For the POC success criteria gating — if Hosted meets p95/p99 targets and security checklist passes, we move to product integration. If Hosted fails latency gates but Dedicated meets them, we consider Dedicated procurement. If neither meets them, we escalate to Private.
[07:02] Mateo Ruiz: Correct. That's our recommended decision ladder.
[07:08] Tom Gallagher: About cost, can you give an example of delta between hosted and dedicated? Even rough numbers help our finance model.
[07:14] Alicia Park: We'll provide sample cost models. Roughly, Dedicated reduces per-token cost under predictable, sustained load because you amortize reserved capacity — but it requires a commit. Hosted avoids commit but is higher per-unit at scale. We'll send a modeling spreadsheet.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Ok great. Any gotchas in the benchmark?
[07:33] Mateo Ruiz: A few: 1) sequence length distribution matters a lot — 600 vs 200 tokens changes compute drastically; 2) function calling or multi-turn context increases memory/KV pressure; 3) quantization and model choice change latency/cost tradeoffs. We'll propose a small matrix of model variants to test.
[07:49] Ethan Lowe: Can we run a quick dry-run this week? Even a small 1-hour hosted baseline with a 10k request sample?
[07:55] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we can run a 1-hour baseline once we get an anonymized sample. I can start the run in 24–48 hours after we receive the artifacts.
[08:03] Tom Gallagher: I'll aim to get the sample by Friday (2026-12-24) but want to flag that our security team will be out on X-mas eve — Sara will coordinate.
[08:12] Sara Kim: Yes, we can target the 24th for a preliminary dump, but final scrub might slip to Jan 4.
[08:18] Alicia Park: Noted. We'll plan the formal 2-week replay for early Jan.
[08:22] Priya Nair: Anything we should watch for with the p99 measurement? We've had issues where the p99 spiked because of external DB calls.
[08:29] Mateo Ruiz: If external dependencies affect latency, please capture those spans or isolate the model-serving path in traces. Our harness can replay just the model calls but you'll need to indicate external system timings.
[08:41] Ethan Lowe: For the pilot, we'd like Redwood to capture token-level cost and per-route latency so we can map features to cost. Is that available in the Console?
[08:50] Alicia Park: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakout and per-route dashboards. We'll give demo credentials as part of the follow-up.
[08:58] Tom Gallagher: On SLA: for dedicated customers what's typical uptime SLA?
[09:03] Mateo Ruiz: Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed uptime (depending on contract) — 99.9% or higher is possible with multi-zone setups. We'll include SLA language in the SOW.
[09:12] Priya Nair: Any implications for model version pinning during the POC? We need deterministic outputs for evaluation.
[09:18] Mateo Ruiz: You can pin model versions and we support rollout controls. For the POC, we'll pin to a single model and snapshot the weights to ensure determinism.
[09:27] Alicia Park: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:30] Alicia Park: Action: Mateo to share benchmark harness and scripts by 2026-12-23.
[09:36] Mateo Ruiz: Will do.
[09:37] Alicia Park: Tom & Sara to provide anonymized traces; target initial sample by 2026-12-24 and full scrubbed 2-week trace by 2027-01-04.
[09:44] Tom Gallagher: Confirmed.
[09:45] Priya Nair: We'll look at whether Private needs to be in scope; decision by 2027-01-07.
[09:51] Alicia Park: Redwood to send SOW template, SAML guide, security evidence pack and initial pricing by 2026-12-22.
[09:58] Alicia Park: Any more questions?
[10:02] Ethan Lowe: One small ask — can you include an example of a burst policy config for Dedicated so we can show infra?
[10:07] Mateo Ruiz: Yep, will include burst policy examples and region routing rules.
[10:11] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone, that was useful.
[10:14] Alicia Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:18] [crosstalk, some voices overlapping, short goodbyes] 
[56:30] End of recording
